chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Hal Leroy and borrowed steps
summary: Hal Leroy looked up to his dancing, but Bubbles says he could answer any step with another so the audience would not notice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: What about some of the people who were in that show with you, like Hal Leroy. I take it he looked up to
you, he was influenced by you.
My dancing ability. I kept beating out -- keep the whole (inaudible) going, that's what he was on me about. Yeah.
Did you find that he was copying any of the things that you were doing or taking any of the things that you were -- or any other people were --

I don't know what he was taking, I didn't pay no attention. I wasn't worried about that, because why is he going to do it. When it's ready to be done he could do it right in front of me but I'd do another step of the same thing and the audience won't know the difference. He could do a step in front of me or the step that I did and I could do that same step right after he gets through with it and you couldn't recognize the
step. You just know it's a good step, that's all. That's all I want it to be, a good step, see?
